text:
Sam: hit a small but repeatable hang in staging: prefetch worker and eviction sweep form a circular wait under high demote churn. minimal stack pasted.
Priya: can you paste the stack/gist?
Sam: gist: ```prefetch.acquire(shard_lock)
evict.acquire(tenant_lock)
evict.wait(prefetch_release)
prefetch.wait(evict_quiesce) // circular```
Omar: looks like lock-order inversion (shard vs tenant). three paths: 1) reorder locks globally, 2) optimistic lease-transfer RPC, 3) RW tenant lock (shared for prefetch, exclusive for eviction).
Yuki: optimistic lease-transfer = eviction sends TransferRequest(tenant,prefix,req_id) and prefetch either hands off or NACKs. requires holder_generation and idempotency.
Jessie: reordering locks is simplest but may widen prefetch critical section and hurt tail-latency. we should bench.
Priya: RW tenant lock needs upgrade-safe semantics; naive upgrade can deadlock. try-lock+backoff or coordinator token needed.
Sam: near-term mitigation: bounded acquire for eviction (X ms), then requeue with exponential backoff. prevents full system stall while we design fix.
Omar: agree. also add small telemetry: capture sampled "waiter_path" when goroutine blocks >10ms (list of locks held). helps detect cycles before outages.
Yuki: proto sketch for transfer: ```rpc TransferPrefix(req_id, tenant, prefix) returns {status, holder_gen, holder_info}``` comment: "handoff must be idempotent and tolerate retries."
Jessie: note failure modes: prefetch crash during handoff, partial commit, duplicate transfer. need lease epoch checks and GC of stale holders.
evict-bot: created INF-2499: "staging: prefix transfer deadlock" and INF-2500: "telemetry: waiter_path sampling"
Sam: owners: Omar bounded-wait patch, Yuki transfer proto doc, Priya RW-lock prototype + tests, Jessie bench reordering impact. reconvene after benches.
Priya: will add unit tests covering upgrade races.
Omar: starting bounded-wait patch now, will stage canary with lower eviction budget.
Jessie: i'll run microbench for reorder vs transfer vs RW-lock and post numbers later today.
Sam: thanks all. keep thread small and paste links to PRs and bench CSVs.
